subject: physical-education
title: Synthesis and review: trail, road, and shared-space etiquette under transfer
essentialQuestion: What does it take to be active outside safely and repeatedly?
privacySafeScenario: Plan and complete one guardian-approved outdoor activity, including the safety plan, and produce a map of free activity spaces reachable from home.
studentTask: Learner works trail, road, and shared-space etiquette on an outing the learner plans and leads through, where the weather, terrain, or timing does not cooperate at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of trail, road, and shared-space etiquette degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner holds trail, road, and shared-space etiquette on an outing the learner plans and leads through, where the weather, terrain, or timing does not cooperate, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
adaptationChoices: Distance, duration, terrain, and pace are learner-set. An indoor or home-yard equivalent is available in full for any learner for whom outdoor activity is unsafe, inaccessible, or not approved.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of trail, road, and shared-space etiquette yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Distance, duration, terrain, and pace are learner-set. An indoor or home-yard equivalent is available in full for any learner for whom outdoor activity is unsafe, inaccessible, or not approved.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where trail, road, and shared-space etiquette shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
